cohort: 150 antenatal women diagnosed with placental abruption admitted to the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Government Hospital Kakinada.
finding: Risk factors for placental abruption included multiparity, advanced maternal age, low socioeconomic status, nutritional anemia, hypertensive disorders, multiple pregnancy, polyhydramnios, prior abruption, uterine malformations, premature rupture of membranes, trauma, fibroids, thrombophilia, and smoking; the majority of women delivered by cesarean section, postpartum hemorrhage and blood transfusions were common, and maternal and neonatal mortality were 2.6% and 1.5%, respectively.
mod_finding: 75% of the women delivered by cesarean section.
